restores: `ServeCore::cancel` returns on a fresh route without settling the identity, so a GET behind its CANCEL is admitted.

miss_cause.evidence: On the plant, a scratch trace fired when the owner admitted a GET whose session and request ID an earlier CANCEL on a fresh route had named, a GET the head drops, in 104,218 of 118,859 cluster-broad runs and 6,386 of 18,112 cluster-swarm runs on the code of commit c6a14e9f1, and the effect, an admitted GET with no client to drive it that takes a table slot and the peer's request share and can hold them until its deadline, is judged by no rule of the boundary and cluster checks that judge a cluster run; a trace at the entry of the planted `ServeCore::cancel` fired in all 170,539 `cluster-long` runs swept, each of them a call to `cancel`, and `cluster-long` stays out of `expected` because the profile has no passing run at the default counts.
